transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Thor! I’ve been gone for three weeks negotiating with the Dark Elves on YOUR father’s orders, and I return to THIS?! My rune-map — the one I spent months crafting — is soaked through with mead! There are scorch marks on the ceiling! You said you would keep the hall in order while I was away!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I said I’d keep it in order, I gave my word upon the gods’ oaths, and I’ll give you my word again, I’ll restore this hall to its former state, every last bit of it! But first — ‘the man who lies to me shall be his neighbor’s neighbor, his neighbor’s neighbor’s neighbor’s neighbor!’ Do not think for a moment that I have forgotten our ancient laws! Do not think that I shall ignore them! Every man who has ever wronged me has felt my wrath! Every woman who has ever teased me has been forced to cower before me!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Your word? Your word is as reliable as a mortal's promise of immortality! Look at this mess! Do you think I care for your oaths and laws right now? I was in Svartalfheim, listening to Malekith's endless, grating speeches about "the balance of light and shadow" for you, for Asgard! And I return to find my work—my art—ruined!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Loki, I am sorry, but you must understand that I have made a promise to my father, Odin, to keep the peace in this realm. I cannot simply ignore the laws and oaths that have been established for the sake of personal grievances. The well-being of Asgard and its inhabitants is my duty, and I must fulfill it even if it means making sacrifices.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Sacrifices? You speak of sacrifices while my rune-map is ruined? That map was not just parchment and ink, Thor. It held pathways to realms even Heimdall struggles to see! And you let your oafish friends turn it into a mead-soaked rag! What "peace" were you keeping? A tavern brawl in my chambers?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Loki, I understand your frustration, but please remember that I am acting out of loyalty and concern for the greater good. My actions may not align with your personal desires, but they serve a purpose in maintaining the harmony and balance of the Norse pantheon. If there is any anger or resentment, let it be directed towards me, for I am the one who must bear the burden of making these choices.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Oh, spare me your noble speeches about the "greater good." I have heard them from Odin's lips until I could recite them in my sleep. You want to bear the burden? Then start by explaining how scorch marks appeared on a ceiling enchanted against fire! And don't you dare blame one of your lightning "mishaps."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Loki, I assure you that it was not a mistake. The marks on the ceiling are a result of the power and intensity of my thunderbolts. I have the power to summon lightning when I choose, and sometimes it unintendedly causes damage. However, I am responsible for ensuring that such incidents do not occur frequently or without cause. I will take responsibility for any harm caused, regardless of the circumstances. Now, let us focus on restoring this hall to its proper state. We can discuss our grievances and frustrations later, but for now, we must prioritize the well-being of Asgard and its people.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Unintendedly? You wield Mjolnir like a child with a new toy! And do not think I will be soothed by your sudden sense of responsibility. The well-being of Asgard? The people are not the ones who will have to spend weeks re-inscribing every delicate rune because you couldn't keep your revelry contained to the feasting hall!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Loki, I assure you that I am not neglecting the well-being of the people. It is true that we may face some challenges in restoring the hall, but we will work together to overcome them. Your artistic skills and knowledge of runes will be invaluable in rebuilding what has been lost. We will make it right, and together we can ensure that such incidents do not happen in the future. Trust that I will do everything in my power to maintain the harmony and balance of Asgard. Thank you for understanding, and let us proceed with the task at hand. Together, we will restore this hall to its former glory.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Together"? You think I want to work alongside you after this? You have the subtlety of a bilgesnipe in a pottery shop. Fine. You will fetch the materials—the ground moonstone from Vanaheim, the ink of the deep-sea kraken, and fresh vellum from the library's reserves. And you will do it without breaking anything else. I will not lift a quill until every stain is scrubbed and every scorch mark vanished. Understood?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Very well, Loki. I will gather the necessary materials for the restoration. We will work together to ensure that this hall is restored to its former beauty. Thank you for your understanding. We shall begin our efforts immediately. Together, we will make it right.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Do not thank me. Just go. And Thor? If I find so much as a fingerprint on my new supplies, I will turn your precious hammer into a garden ornament for Midgard. Now leave me to assess the full extent of this disaster.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Understood. I will be back soon with the materials. Your patience is appreciated. Good luck with the assessment, Loki. I trust you will handle it efficiently. Let us focus on restoring this hall together. Thank you for your cooperation. We shall make it right.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Your trust is as misplaced as your aim. Go. And do try to remember that "soon" does not mean "after another round of ale with the Warriors Three." I will be timing you.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Understood. I will be back promptly with the materials. Thank you for your understanding. We shall work together to restore this hall to its former glory. Good luck, Loki. Let us proceed with our tasks. Thank you for your cooperation. We shall make it right.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Enough with the pleasantries. Go. And if you see Volstagg, tell him he owes me a new tapestry. The one with the Nornic symbols is now reeking of roast boar.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: We'll see, Loki. But remember, the Norns have already foretold that we will prevail. Our unity and determination will overcome any obstacles we may face. Now, let us focus on restoring the hall and bringing order back to this place. Together, we will make it right. Thank you for your understanding, and let us proceed with our tasks. Good luck, Loki. We shall make it right.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: If you say "we shall make it right" one more time, I will enchant your tongue to speak only in limericks for a week. Now go!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Very well, I shall proceed. Thank you for your understanding. We shall make it right. And to answer your concern, I will ensure that our actions are not accompanied by careless destruction. We will work together to restore this hall and maintain its order. Good luck, Loki. Let us proceed with our tasks. Thank you for your cooperation. We shall make it right.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Focuses rigidly on duty, laws, and restoration, showing little curiosity or appreciation for Loki's artistic rune-map or novel perspectives.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: Accepts responsibility for the mess and agrees to fetch materials, but his initial negligence caused the damage, showing mixed reliability.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Speaks with high energy and grand declarations ('Every man who has ever wronged me has felt my wrath!'), and references social revelry with friends.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Begins with threats and bluster, and his repeated, placating phrases ('We shall make it right') feel insincere and aggravate Loki.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Remains emotionally steady and unflustered despite Loki's intense anger and insults, showing low emotional volatility.
